sentences: SETH, the APSP hypothesis, and the 3SUM hypothesis assert precise barriers for three different computational tasks.
The source asks whether at least one of these hypotheses must be true.
This disjunction is weaker than proving any particular member, because it permits the others to fail.
A proof would give a robust foundation for results whose conditional hardness follows from whichever barrier survives.
The saved historical formulation still depends on the exact machine, numeric, and randomness conventions of its three constituents, so mixing incompatible versions would change the proposition.
